blocks.text: The language of mercy and grace in verses 8–13 belongs to a wider biblical world of covenant life, worship, kingship, wisdom teaching, and prophetic critique. These settings provide background for the psalm’s description of Jehovah as merciful, gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in lovingkindness, while the psalm itself remains the controlling witness.

The mercy and grace celebrated in verses 8–13 are themes read across the canon, developing from Israel’s story into the New Testament witness. Psalm 103 therefore stands within a broader scriptural treatment of divine mercy rather than presenting an isolated description.
